method: Read review-rubric.md, rig.py, kettlebell.py, motions.py (kb-deadlift, goblet-squat, reverse-lunge), kb_advanced.py and contracts.json. Inspected all 14 contact sheets (4 views x 8 phases; 16 phases for get-up) and enlarged frames for kb-deadlift 0.0 threequarter, goblet-squat 0.5 threequarter, kb-halo 0.125 threequarter, kb-clean 0.5 front, kb-getup 0.375 threequarter / 0.5 left / 0.5625 front. Used geometry.json for bone, grip, support, seam and drawn-radius clearances. Probed pose_for() in python3: knee, elbow and hip angles, forearm tilt, bell-to-head distance, and a whole-body centre of mass from Dempster-style segment fractions (70 kg body + 16 kg bell) against the contact polygon. Bone lengths, grip attachment, support drift, floor and loop seam pass validation for every clip. Not exercised: real playback, so timing, velocity and momentum are inferred from the authoring curves only. Head/trunk-vs-bell clearance and the dynamic (centripetal) bell load were estimated by hand, not measured by a validator. The COM model is approximate, so balance findings within about 2 cm of an edge are medium confidence.

kb-swing.summary: The hinge-to-stand pattern, planted feet and long arms are credible. But the forearms pass deep into the thighs at the backswing, and the float has no counterbalance, so the bell looks close to weightless.

defects.issue: Forearms and upper arms interpenetrate the thighs (forearm vs thigh -8.8 cm, upper arm -2.1 cm with drawn radii). The arms pass through the legs instead of meeting the inner thigh or groin.
defects.fix: Move the hands above the knees and between the thighs (a higher, tighter hike), or widen the knees and stance so the forearms contact the inner thigh with clearance of 0 or more.

defects.issue: At the chest-height float the body is perfectly vertical with the bell 0.66 m forward. Combined COM is +0.149 m against a toe edge of +0.16 m. With centripetal pull the lifter would tip forward. There is no counter-lean or hip-forward plank.
defects.fix: Add a slight posterior lean of about 3-6 degrees (pelvis slightly forward of the ankles, shoulders slightly behind) at the float so the COM stays mid-foot.

defects.issue: Hinge and arm angle are both driven by the same symmetric pulse. The descent exactly mirrors the ascent, and the hips start folding while the arms are still about 55 degrees up (early hinge). There is no visible 'wait for the bell' or deceleration into the backswing.
defects.fix: Decouple the timing: keep the hips extended until the forearms reach the pelvis on the way down, then hinge quickly. Make the downswing faster than the float.

kb-deadlift.summary: The start, lift and lockout sequence is readable and feet stay planted. But the arms pass through the thighs and shins at the floor, the bottom position is an extreme fold, and at lockout the bell is held forward instead of hanging.

defects.issue: Upper arms pass through the thighs (-11.0 cm) and forearms through the thighs (-9.4 cm at 0.133). Upper arm vs shin is -7.4 cm at 0.0. These are geometrically impossible overlaps at the most important frame.
defects.fix: Put the arms clearly inside the knees (spread the knees and widen the stance slightly) or move the grip lateral to the knees. The validator should reject negative clearances.

defects.issue: The trunk is 72 degrees from vertical with the knees at 93 degrees, giving a trunk-thigh angle of about 40 degrees. The chest nearly rests on the thighs. This is a squat depth combined with a horizontal torso, not a hip hinge.
defects.fix: Use about 45-55 degrees of trunk lean with less knee flexion (about 110-130 degrees), so the hips are higher and the shoulders sit over the bell.

defects.issue: At lockout the bell sits 0.16 m ahead of the shoulders with straight arms angled forward. That is a front-raise hold, and a hanging load would pull the arms plumb against the thighs.
defects.fix: End with the arms vertical and the bell hanging just in front of or between the thighs. Keep any knee-clearance offset only in mid-lift.

goblet-squat.summary: Credible goblet squat. Heels stay down, the knees track forward over the feet, the trunk lean balances the chest-held load, the combined COM stays mid-foot, and the arms clear the thighs at the bottom.

defects.issue: Minor: the narrow stance (0.30 m) with knees straight ahead makes the upper arms close to the thighs (+1.6 cm). The trunk is one rigid segment, so there is no thoracic extension against the load.
defects.fix: Optional: add a slight knee abduction or turn-out so the elbows sit inside the knees with more margin.

kb-reverse-lunge.summary: Step back, rear forefoot support, lowering and the fixed front foot are all credible, with good knee angles (front about 77, rear about 94 degrees). The return lifts the rear foot while the COM is still over the front heel.

defects.issue: The rear foot leaves the floor while the pelvis is still 0.13 m back. Combined COM is -0.076 m against a front-heel edge of -0.075 m, so the lifter is balanced on the heel edge and the push-off shows no forward weight transfer (mirrored at 0.875).
defects.fix: Shift the pelvis forward over the front mid-foot before or as the rear toe leaves the floor, so the drive comes from the front leg.

kb-side-lunge.summary: Wide-stance lateral shift with a flexed working knee aligned over its foot, a long trailing leg, hips sitting back and the chest-held bell. The COM stays well inside the wide base.

defects.issue: Minor: the trunk is one rigid block with a 15 degree lean and no pelvis rotation toward the working leg, so the sit-back looks slightly stiff.
defects.fix: Optional: add a few degrees of hip rotation and trunk lean over the working thigh.

kb-upright-row.summary: The elbows lead and stay below the shoulders, but the bell travels in a vertical line 0.20 m in front of the body. The arm action is forward shoulder flexion, not an upright row close to the body.

defects.issue: At the bottom the straight arms angle about 20 degrees forward and hold the bell 20 cm in front of the thighs. A hanging bell would pull the arms plumb against the legs.
defects.fix: Start with the arms vertical and the bell hanging against the thighs.

defects.issue: At the top the elbows are 0.27 m in front of the torso (upper arm mostly forward). The bell stays 20 cm off the chest, and there is no trunk counter-lean for that moment arm.
defects.fix: Keep the bell within a few centimetres of the torso along the whole path. Raise the elbows up and out in the scapular plane (upper arm mostly lateral), and pull the handle toward the lower chest.

kb-bent-row.summary: A stable hinge (55 degrees lean, soft knees) with a hanging start. The elbows travel back past the torso beside the ribs and the COM stays over mid-foot. Mechanics are credible.

defects.issue: Minor: the bell touches the thighs (-0.7 cm). The pull ends near the hip crease rather than the lower ribs.
defects.fix: Optional: bring the grip path 2-3 cm forward so the bell clears the thighs and finishes nearer the lower ribs.

kb-side-bend.summary: The bend goes toward the loaded side with planted feet and a stable pelvis, and the handoff grip holds. The loaded arm stays abducted, so the bell hangs away from the leg and does not read as weight.

defects.issue: The loaded arm is held about 17 degrees abducted (world-space FK, outward 0.30), so the bell hangs well outside the thigh during the bend. A heavy bell would pull the arm plumb against the side of the leg.
defects.fix: Let the loaded arm hang vertical from the shoulder in world space, with the bell beside the outer thigh sliding toward the knee as the trunk bends.

defects.issue: All lateral flexion happens at one pelvis-chest hinge. There is no small contralateral hip shift to keep the COM centred.
defects.fix: Add a 1-3 cm pelvis shift away from the bell as the trunk bends.

kb-curl.summary: Elbow-only flexion with a quiet upper arm, a bell hanging below the handle, and a credible transfer grip. The working arm stays abducted away from the body under load.

defects.issue: Both arms stay about 17 degrees abducted (outward 0.30), so the bell hangs out to the side at the bottom and curls in a tilted plane. A loaded arm would hang with the elbow against the ribs.
defects.fix: Reduce the working-arm abduction to about 5 degrees at the bottom, with the elbow pinned near the flank throughout the curl.

kb-halo.summary: The fixed-length arms circle the head with straight wrists and continuous horn grips, and the shoulders elevate when the elbows rise. Bell, arms and head clear each other (bell to head centre at least 0.214 m, forearm to head at least 0.153 m).

defects.issue: Minor: the trunk and neck stay perfectly still as the bell passes behind the head, with no bracing or small forward counter-lean. The load reads light.
defects.fix: Optional: add a 1-2 degree forward trunk counter-lean as the bell passes behind the head.

kb-clean.summary: The phase order and rack are credible, but the single-arm backswing drives the bell and forearm through the left thigh and shin. The pull flares the elbow wide, and the free arm does not hang.

defects.issue: The bell interpenetrates the left thigh (-12.8 cm) and shin (-8.9 cm at 0.333). Forearm vs thigh is -9.9 cm and hand vs thigh -8.5 cm. The bell is visibly buried in the leg at the backswing.
defects.fix: Route the single-arm backswing through the midline between the knees, with the wrist near the groin. Widen the stance if needed, and require clearance of 0 or more in QA.

defects.issue: During the pull to the rack the elbow flares 0.20 m outside the shoulder (upper arm about 45 degrees lateral). The contract cue is 'elbow back and in', and a flare throws the bell around the arm.
defects.fix: Keep the elbow close to the ribs and moving backward, with the hand tracking up the body before it rotates around the bell.

defects.issue: In the hinge the free arm points forward and down about 33 degrees from vertical (world-space FK plus the hinge term) instead of hanging or counterbalancing.
defects.fix: Let the free arm hang plumb from the shoulder, or mirror the working arm slightly behind as a counterbalance.

kb-press.summary: The rack and the lockout (biceps by the ear, bell on the back of the forearm) are credible. Through the mid-range the forearm is far off vertical and the elbow points straight out sideways, so the load is off the line of force.

defects.issue: The forearm is 65 degrees from vertical, with the upper arm pointing almost purely lateral (direction y 0.84) and the wrist medial near the face. This contradicts the intended 'forearm vertical under the bell' and implies a huge shoulder torque (mirrored at 0.75-0.82).
defects.fix: Keep the wrist stacked over the elbow through the whole press, with the elbow about 30-45 degrees forward of the frontal plane and the hand path just outside the face.

defects.issue: In the rack the forearm is tilted 37 degrees with the wrist inside the elbow, so it is not the vertical forearm, tucked elbow and bell resting in the arm/chest pocket.
defects.fix: Make the rack forearm near vertical, with the elbow on the ribcage under the wrist.

kb-snatch.summary: The turnover, hip drive, high pull and punch-through sequence is present, with a credible lockout. The backswing buries the bell in the left thigh, and the punch-through grazes the head.

defects.issue: Bell vs left thigh is -13.2 cm. Forearm vs thigh -9.8 cm and hand vs thigh -8.4 cm at 0.50-0.51, and bell vs shin -3.7 cm at 0.525. These are impossible overlaps at the backswing.
defects.fix: Use the same fix as the clean: route the bell through the midline between the knees and hike it high to the groin, then re-validate clearances.

defects.issue: On the punch-through the bell centre passes 0.159 m from the head centre. With a 0.095 m bell radius and a head half-width of about 0.08 m, that is about 2 cm of bell-head interpenetration (between the sampled 0.75 and 0.875 frames).
defects.fix: Push the punch-through path about 3 cm more lateral or forward of the head, and add bell-vs-head to the clearance validator.

kb-getup.summary: The bell arm stays vertical and the floor pins are exact, but several transitions are not physically possible. The stand-up happens on one foot with the COM outside the base, the sweeping leg passes through the support arm, and the elbow-support stage never touches the floor.

defects.issue: From 0.52 to 0.58 the rear knee leaves the floor and the right foot is airborne (ankle 0.18-0.24 m high) while the pelvis rises. The only support is the left foot at y +0.17 while the combined COM is at y -0.11 to -0.02. The lifter would fall sideways. Same error on the way down at about 0.69-0.74.
defects.fix: Keep the rear knee then the rear toes planted while rising out of the half-kneel (a lunge stand). Shift the COM over the front foot before either rear contact unloads, and step the rear foot up only once the COM is over the front foot.

defects.issue: During the leg sweep the right upper arm passes through the shin (-8.3 cm) and thigh (-7.7 cm), and the forearm through the shin (-6.5 cm). The knee rises to 0.65 m instead of threading low under the hips (mirrored at about 0.81).
defects.fix: Sweep the straight leg back under the bridged hips along the floor, behind the posted arm, keeping the knee low and clear of the support arm.

defects.issue: The authored 'elbow' key (0.15) never grounds the elbow (elbow joint 0.12 m above the floor). The trunk is held up on a bent arm with only a palm contact, so the roll-to-elbow support stage is missing.
defects.fix: Pin the right forearm or elbow to the floor during the elbow stage, then transition to the posted hand.

defects.issue: The kneeling rear shin is horizontal while the foot points forward under the shin, about 36 degrees beyond neutral dorsiflexion. At exactly 0.5 the knee contact is dropped from the contact list although the knee is still on the floor.
defects.fix: Orient the rear foot vertical with the toes tucked behind the ankle, and keep the knee in the contact set through the whole kneel hold.
